Engine work around East Hartford: will your NDT certificate sit under SNT-TC-1A or NAS 410?

East Hartford is an engine town. Pratt & Whitney has its headquarters and main US manufacturing here, its Middletown plant sits down the Connecticut River, Collins Aerospace makes aircraft systems in Windsor Locks, and Sikorsky builds heavy-lift helicopters in Stratford. Around them, central Connecticut is full of shops that forge, cast, machine, coat and repair engine parts. For an NDT technician the answer to the scheme question usually comes from a document nobody shows you on day one: the purchase order between your employer and its customer.

How each scheme reaches a Hartford County shop

NAS 410 is an Aerospace Industries Association standard. It turns mandatory when a contract, purchase order or customer quality clause invokes it. Engine and airframe makers commonly write it, or EN 4179, its European twin, into the quality clauses they send to suppliers, and each supplier passes the clause down to whoever inspects the hardware. A Connecticut Valley forging house can end up certifying its inspectors to NAS 410 because of wording drafted two or three companies up the chain.

SNT-TC-1A, the ASNT recommended practice, arrives by another road. An employer adopts it in a written practice, and ASME, API and AWS documents give it force. Around Hartford that covers structural and pressure fabricators, bridge and rail contractors, power plants, and nuclear in-service inspection at Millstone in Waterford, which follows ASME Section XI and the ASNT documents that code calls for. A technician in this region can easily work under both schemes over a career, sometimes inside one company.

Rotating parts and the ultrasonic technician

Disks, shafts and other rotating engine parts start life as billet and forgings, and a large share of corridor ultrasonic work is immersion and contact scanning of that material before it is machined. Fluorescent penetrant follows on finished surfaces, and eddy current is used on holes and slots. A missed indication on a rotating part is the failure every engine customer fears, so auditors look hard at who signed each result and why that person was qualified.

Coming over from weld UT or thickness surveys? The shop's Responsible Level 3 (RL3) will weigh your earlier training and experience against its own NAS 410 written practice and decide what to credit. An SNT-TC-1A certificate is evidence of what you have done; it does not satisfy a NAS 410 requirement by itself. Expect the gap to show in penetrant and magnetic particle, where NAS 410 asks for more formal, documented training than SNT-TC-1A recommends. The forging and casting UT guide shows what that inspection involves.

What to keep so a Connecticut RL3 can credit you

  • Course records that show the outline, the hours and the instructor, not only a completion certificate.
  • An experience log signed by a supervisor or Level 3, split by method and by product form: forgings, castings, machined parts, welds.
  • Your general, specific and practical examination history, with the procedure and specification each practical used.
  • Near-vision and color-perception records.
  • Each certification letter, showing the standard and the revision it was issued under.

Leave the employer and the certification lapses. The file is what moves with you to the next shop.

For quality managers at central Connecticut suppliers

Many shops here carry aerospace and industrial orders side by side. Keep the two programs visibly apart, name the governing standard and revision on every certification letter, and plan the update of your NAS 410 written practice to Revision 6, released in December 2025, as your customers call for it. A Nadcap AC7114 auditor will trace each technician from the signed report back through training, experience, examination and vision records, and a thin file becomes a finding. Atlantis offers NAS 410 audit documentation support for Hartford-area suppliers: we prepare and review those files, and your RL3 approves them.

Where Atlantis fits in the engine corridor

Atlantis training is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A: self-paced online theory with Q&A from our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), rehearsal in the aircraft hangar and NDT lab scenes of the Practical NDT simulator, then the hands-on work and practical examination at your employer's facility under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in East Hartford. For aerospace employers we build SNT-TC-1A-based written practices aligned to customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114, write procedures, administer Level I and II examinations and serve as outside agency ASNT Level III. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to East Hartford employers or anyone else. Whether outside coursework counts toward a NAS 410 certification at an engine-parts shop is for that shop's RL3 to decide, so ask before you enroll. The NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A comparison sets the two documents side by side, and the East Hartford aerospace NDT training page covers the course routes.
